identification: Acrylic painting of a curled, sleeping thylacine (Tasmanian tiger) in a roughly 25 cm circular reserve, painted directly onto a polished natural-edge burl slab (likely Tasmanian timber burl, bark edge left on), wall-hung, about 60 x 57 cm overall. Catalogued as by Alison Cooper-White, a living Launceston artist (portraits, pets, Tasmanian animals painted on recycled and antique wood, Huon pine, old boxes and drawers; sells at Evandale Market, on Bluethumb and her own site; very active on Facebook/Instagram with thylacine pieces in Aug to Oct 2026). Current bid A$330, estimate 500-600.
marks_seen: No signature visible on the front in any of the 3 photos (zoomed the painted roundel and edges). Presumably signed or labelled on the back, not photographed. Armitage tag only.
google_searches: Alison Cooper-White artist; Alison Cooper-White thylacine; Alison Cooper-White burl painting Tasmania

resale_estimate: A$250-450. A Tasmanian or tourist buyer through a Launceston/Hobart gallery-style shop or Marketplace might pay up to A$450; at a general auction or eBay auction it is more like A$150-300. No secondary-market record for the artist.
doubts: No auction or resale record for Alison Cooper-White anywhere (artrecord.com, LiveAuctioneers, eBay sold, Google). She is a living local artist who sells direct at markets, and she is posting thylacine pieces on wood right now, so the market can be resupplied. Armitage has sold her work before (a pine trunk with a hand-painted thylacine, estimate A$500-700), which hints she or a collector consigns to Armitage; the other bidders may be her local following. No signature visible on the front in the photos; it may be on the back. At the current A$330 bid plus 22% premium you are already paying about A$403, above most resale outcomes.
viewing_check: Look for her signature (front edge or back) and any label with title or date. Check the burl for cracks, checking or splits across the slab, borer holes and a stable finish; identify the timber (Huon pine, myrtle or blackwood burl would help the price). Check the hanging fixing on the back.

identification: Kenneth Jack (1924-2006) 'Elmore, Victoria' 1992, watercolour on paper, image about 42.5 x 77 cm, in a gilt frame with cream mat. Main street of Elmore with two-storey red brick building at left, verandahed shops, street light, big willow at right, flock of birds, dry grass foreground. The Australian Art Sales Digest (AASD) lists exactly this composition (matching thumbnail: red brick building left, willow right, grass foreground) as 'Elmore, Victoria 1992, watercolour on paper, signed and dated lower right Kenneth Jack/ 1992, signed and inscribed on backing verso: Elmore (Victoria)/ Kenneth Jack R. W. S, 42.5 x 77 cm', sold at an earlier auction alongside its companion 'Kerang, Victoria 1992' (50.5 x 71 cm). Same title and the exact catalogue dimensions (H-42 W-77) make it very likely this is that original, not a print.
marks_seen: Photo 1 (800x600, close-up) and photo 2 (800x600, whole frame). Signature lower right in the grass, dark small script, consistent with 'Kenneth Jack' with a date but not legible at this resolution. No pencil signature or edition number visible on the mat area (a print's pencil signature would sit on the paper margin, which the mat may cover). Small white sticker top right of the mat, illegible (probably an auction or gallery tag). A narrow strip of paper shows between the image edge and the mat window, with a crisp straight image edge; that alone does not settle original vs print as Jack often masked his edges. Sky gradation looks painted (deep blue to pale at the horizon).
google_searches: "Kenneth Jack" "Elmore" (Google: found AASD record of the original 1992 watercolour 42.5 x 77 cm with verso inscription); Kenneth Jack Elmore watercolour or print (web); Kenneth Jack Candelo watercolour Lawsons. Kenneth Jack did issue offset lithographs and limited-edition lithos of country-town subjects (e.g. Moonrise at Beechworth offset litho, Clunes Victoria colour litho 43 x 69 cm), so a reproduction is possible in principle, but no print edition of Elmore turned up.
existing_max_note: Max A$500 only if original Kenneth Jack. Estimate 800-1500, no bids yet at time of check (opening A$400).

resale_estimate: As an original 1992 watercolour, 42.5 x 77 cm: A$500-800 hammer at Leonard Joel or Gibson's (between the A$420-500 paid for 36 x 58 cm town scenes and the A$800 for a 67 x 100 cm Country Town). If it turned out to be a print: A$80-150.
doubts: Verdict supports: A$500 hammer (A$610 with 22% BP) is about the bottom of the realistic resale range for an original of this size, so the margin after selling costs (roughly 20-25% at Leonard Joel or Gibson's) is thin, close to break-even at A$500-600 resale and only good if it makes A$700-800. Kenneth Jack watercolours have softened, most medium works sell at or under low estimate (A$320-500). The AASD match is by title, size and thumbnail composition; I could not see the AASD sale date or price (paywalled). Glass reflections and the 800x600 photos stop me reading the signature date. The Candelo comp is unverified.
viewing_check: Take the frame off the wall and look at the back: the original is recorded as 'signed and inscribed on backing verso: Elmore (Victoria)/ Kenneth Jack R. W. S'. If that inscription is there, it is the original. Front: signature 'Kenneth Jack/ 1992' lower right should be in paint, not printed; under a loupe or angled light, watercolour shows paper texture, pigment pooling and pencil underdrawing, a print shows a dot screen or flat uniform colour. If it is the original, A$500 max is fine; if it is a print, A$60-80 max.
searches_tried: Google exact-phrase search; AASD works-on-paper listing (record only, prices paywalled); Invaluable Kenneth Jack sold pages 1-8 (about 380 lots, filtered for sold watercolours), with prices verified on Gibson's and Leonard Joel's own lot pages; Google for Candelo comp. eBay not used (originals of this level rarely sell there; prints only).

identification: Geoffrey (Geoff) Dyer (1947-2020, Hobart, Archibald Prize 2003), 'Still Water Study', watercolour and gouache on paper, image about 31 x 39 cm, cream mat, thin gilt metal frame. Grey-ochre still river or lagoon with dark bush banks, scratched and dragged white gouache, vertical drip lines and dark blots. The handling (gestural wet washes, white gouache scraping, ink drips, muted Tasmanian river palette) is consistent with Dyer's river and Gordon/Franklin studies on paper.
marks_seen: Photo 1 (whole frame on a rug) and photo 2 (closer, 800x600), enlarged 3x. Small signature lower right in the image, reads as 'Dyer' followed by what may be a short date (e.g. '87'), not fully legible. Handwritten paper label on the lower left of the mat reading about '5401/3' with a second word below, looks like a vendor or stock code. No gallery label visible on the front; back not photographed.

resale_estimate: A$800-1,500 hammer at Lawsons or Leonard Joel (the 36 x 40 cm watercolour and gouache made A$1,500 on 28 Oct 2026; a 74 x 18 cm mixed media made A$900 in Dec 2023). Allow for the sale market having softened and this one being slightly smaller: realistic A$900-1,200.
doubts: Verdict raises: the A$500 max was set off one sale; the closest same-medium same-size result (Lawsons, 2 weeks ago) is A$1,500 hammer and Dyer works on paper of every size have been making A$900-2,100 in 2023-2026. Even after 22% BP and 20-25% selling costs, buying at A$800 leaves a margin if it makes A$1,200+. Risks: signature not fully legible in the photos; the back is unseen (no gallery label confirmed); Dyer was prolific and some small studies sell poorly at general sales (Davidson estimated a 27 x 36 cm one at only A$400-600). No evidence of Dyer fakes turned up, and the hand looks right.
viewing_check: Confirm the signature lower right reads 'Dyer' with a date, painted in the same wet medium (not printed). Check the back for a gallery label (Despard, Handmark, Gould, Colville Street etc.) or a title inscription. Look for foxing, mould or cockling in the paper and fading. If signature and paper are good, raise max to about A$800 hammer (A$976 with BP); A$900 at most.
